result:
I found no blocking problems. The spec is mostly strong, with seven findings to settle before it moves to `ready/`. I checked each one against the repo and read every page cited below, including its "When this backfires" section.

## What's already right

- **The criteria test behaviour, not files.** Examples: planted errors must make the lint fail, and `documentSymbol` must return section ranges in a new session. So any wrong facts from the research subagent (such as `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in `args`, or `server` vs `serve`) get caught at verification. This is Level 5 of the fix list in `patterns/anti-patterns/assumption-propagation.md`.
- **The Context holds only what an agent can't find in the repo.** That covers why rumdl `fmt` conflicts with oxfmt, why `rumdl import` fails, and how `references` depends on the cursor (`context-engineering/discoverable-vs-nondiscoverable-context.md`).
- **The criteria follow the repo's own rules.** ADR 0001 says changing a tool needs a new ADR, and criterion 1 asks for one.

## Findings

**1. Worktrees probably won't have `node_modules/`, so criterion 9 (and part of 8) likely can't pass as written.** (Environment layer)
- `node_modules/` is a bind mount on the main checkout only (`mountpoint node_modules` confirms it). `.claude/worktrees/` is gitignored and currently doesn't exist.
- Symlinks are dropped on this mount, so a worktree can't link back to the main `node_modules/`.
- In a worktree, `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/node_modules/rumdl/bin/rumdl` will likely be missing. The existing hooks in `.claude/settings.json` use the same path for `tsx`, so worktree sessions may already be broken. I haven't seen that happen; it's a guess.
- Fix: say in the Context how a worktree gets `node_modules/`, or narrow the criterion. `workflows/agent-environment-bootstrapping.md` recommends setting the environment up deterministically so agents don't find gaps by trial and error. Its backfire case ("proceeds with a partial environment") is exactly an LSP that silently fails to start.

**2. The task bundles two deliverables with different risks.** (Task spec layer)
- Criteria 1–6 and 13 swap the linter in the gate. That's deterministic and verifiable today.
- Criteria 7–12 add the plugin, the session tests and the `docs/tools/` doc. Those depend on a Claude Code bug that was closed unfixed, and on the worktree gap in finding 1.
- If the LSP half stalls, the whole task sits in `blocked/` and holds the implementer's single work slot (`patterns/agent-design/wip-1-littles-law-agent-throughput.md`: "`blocked` keeps the WIP slot held").
- `patterns/anti-patterns/pr-scope-creep-review-bottleneck.md` recommends one logical change per unit. Its backfire (a solo reviewer) only partly applies, because this repo expects many agents working in parallel.
- Suggested split: T-0001 is the lint swap. T-0002 is the plugin, `depends_on: [T-0001]`. The doc could be T-0003, which also fixes finding 3.

**3. Who owns the doc isn't clear in the criteria.** (Task spec / state layer)
- The Context says "the coach writes or reviews the `docs/tools/` doc". But the board allows one `claimed_by` per task, and criterion 11 doesn't say who writes the doc.
- If the coach writes it inside someone else's claimed task, the board can't record that, and the implementer ends up checking part of their own work.
- A separate coach-claimed doc task, depending on the plugin task, keeps separation of duties visible. See the narrow-agents section of `patterns/agent-design/coding-agent-scope-expansion.md`.

**4. The CI check appears only in the Context, not in the criteria.** (Verification layer)
- The Context says to confirm the binary resolves "in CI", but no criterion needs CI evidence. Criterion 13 runs locally only.
- CI does a fresh `npm ci` of platform-specific optional dependencies (`@rumdl/cli-linux-x64`), which is exactly where this can break.
- `workflows/issue-to-pr-delegation-pipeline.md` names underspecified acceptance criteria as the main way delegation fails. `verification/deterministic-guardrails.md` treats CI as its own layer, separate from local checks.
- Fix: add a criterion, or say explicitly that CI is checked after merge.

**5. The planted-error test is a one-time check, and rumdl changes often.** (Verification layer)
- Criterion 4 uses a temporary file, so the proof disappears after the task. The task's own "Churn" note says rumdl releases every few days and will be upgraded later.
- A future upgrade could quietly stop checking cross-file anchors (MD051) or missing files (MD057), and nothing would notice.
- `verification/deterministic-guardrails.md` argues for checks that always run over one-off ones.
- Option: commit a fixture plus a check that asserts the three errors are reported, excluded from the normal `lint:md` run. This is a proposal for the user and the implementer; I can't change tooling.

**6. Two criteria have no command a verifier can run.** (Verification layer)
- Criteria 9 and 10 need "a new Claude Code session", but the board requires each evidence entry to name a `command`. The verifier is another agent and has to reproduce the result.
- Without a named procedure (for example `claude -p` run from the worktree, or `claude --debug` output), there's nothing real to check. This is the "no verification oracle" backfire in `wip-1-littles-law-agent-throughput.md`.
- Fix: name the command in each criterion.

**7. The new doc won't be reachable from `CLAUDE.md`, and its version claims will go stale.** (Context layer)
- `CLAUDE.md` points only to `docs/decisions/`, not to `docs/README.md` or `docs/tools/`. Criterion 12 updates `docs/README.md`, but nothing sends agents there.
- `instructions/agents-md-as-table-of-contents.md` warns in its backfire section that agents don't reliably follow pointers, so a doc that isn't linked from the map is worse still. The fix is a one-line pointer in `CLAUDE.md`, which is my job once the doc exists.
- The doc's "not working as of Claude Code 2.1.282" notes will go stale as Claude Code updates (`patterns/anti-patterns/stale-ai-configuration-artifacts.md`). Its backfire exemption covers pointer-only files, and this doc has concrete version claims, so the warning applies.
- Fix: record a condition for re-checking or removing those notes.
- Also, the Handoff gets rewritten each time a task leaves `active/`. The doc, not the Handoff, should be the lasting record of which operations work.

## Considered but not applicable

- **Plugin supply-chain and pre-trust risks** (`patterns/anti-patterns/install-once-plugin-trust.md`, `security/pre-trust-execution-surface.md`). The plugin is a local directory marketplace committed in git, where auto-update is off by default. This is also a first-party repo in a sandbox, which both pages list as backfire conditions. The existing hooks already run code from `node_modules` at session start, so the plugin adds little new exposure.

## Outside this review

My role file says hooks block `git push` and block Edit/Write outside my output files. But `.claude/settings.json` defines no hook of either kind. Either the role file or the settings are out of date. Changing hooks needs your approval, so I've left it as is.
